deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is writing out a textbook-style theorem on the Schatten–von Neumann classes L^p(H), 0<p≤∞, of operators on a Hilbert space H, with S_p(A)=Σ s_i(A)^p and ||A||_p=S_p(A)^{1/p}. The theorem is stated on the previous page. Part 1 says: (1) ||A||_p=||A*||_p; (2) ||BA||_p ≤ ||B||·||A||_p (two-sided ideal property); (3) ||·||_p is a norm for p≥1; (4) S_p(A+B) ≤ S_p(A)+S_p(B) for 0<p≤1, which makes L^p(H) a complete metrizable TVS, not locally convex for p<1 when dim H=∞. Part 2 is Weyl's inequality Σ|λ_i|^p ≤ S_p(A), together with monotonicity of S_p on positive operators. Part 3 is the Hölder inequality (6): ||AB||_r ≤ ||A||_p||B||_q whenever 1/p+1/q ≥ 1/r.

This page begins the proof.
(i) He first remarks that the topological statements (norm or p-norm, metrizable, complete) follow easily from (3) and (4).
(ii) Formula (1) is evident from the polar decomposition A=U|A| (the fragment 'Riesz)' probably cites F. Riesz). This gives |A*|=U|A|U*, so |A| and |A*| have the same nonzero eigenvalues with multiplicities.
(iii) Formula (2) is the special case q=∞ of (6), but he gives a direct proof. Let (α_i) be the eigenvalues of |A| and (ψ_i) those of |BA|, each in decreasing order and repeated according to multiplicity. Then ψ_i ≤ ||B|| α_i for all i, by the minimax (Courant–Fischer / approximation-number) characterization of singular values. Raising to the p-th power and summing gives (2); the version for AB follows via adjoints and (1).
(iv) Formula (3) for p≥1 is derived from Hölder (6), which will be proved independently, by a duality argument. Take 1/p+1/p'=1 and ||B||_{p'} ≤ 1. Then (6) gives ||AB||_1 ≤ ||A||_p, so |Tr AB| ≤ ||A||_p and sup_{||B||_{p'}≤1}|Tr AB| ≤ ||A||_p.

The next page completes this. It shows the supremum is attained, using the partial isometry U with UA=|A| and a finite-rank H from classical Hölder duality, giving ||A||_p = sup|Tr AB|. Hence ||·||_p is a seminorm, being a supremum of seminorms. For 0<p<1 duality fails, so (4) is to be proved 'par voie analytique' via Lemma 1. For α_i ≥ 0 and f(z)=Π(1+α_i z), the lemma states Σα_i^p = (p sin πp/π) ∫_0^∞ log f(x) x^{-1-p} dx. This presumably reduces (4) to a determinant inequality of the type det(1+x|A+B|) ≤ det(1+x|A|)·det(1+x|B|).
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The inequality ψ_i ≤ ||B||α_i is correct (singular values are approximation numbers, and s_i(BA) ≤ ||B|| s_i(A)).
In (iv) the duality bound is fine. Hölder with 1/p+1/q ≥ 1/r follows from the case of equality plus the monotonicity ||·||_r ≤ ||·||_s for s ≤ r.
The text calls (2) 'a particular case of (6)'. This is the case q=∞, r=p, which is consistent with the statement on the previous page.
Lemma 1 on the next page checks out: ∫_0^∞ log(1+t) t^{-1-p} dt = π/(p sin πp) for 0<p<1, by integration by parts and the Beta integral.

ideas.what: |A| and |A*| have the same nonzero spectrum (via polar decomposition), so ||A||_p=||A*||_p
ideas.modern_name: Polar decomposition; equality of singular values of A and A*
ideas.where_published: Standard (Schatten, 'Norm ideals of completely continuous operators', 1960; Gohberg–Krein 1965)

ideas.what: s_i(BA) ≤ ||B|| s_i(A), giving the ideal inequality ||BA||_p ≤ ||B|| ||A||_p
ideas.where_published: Possibly used in 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956) and 'Produits tensoriels topologiques' (1955); unsure

ideas.what: Triangle inequality for the Schatten p-norm (p≥1) via trace duality ||A||_p = sup_{||B||_{p'}≤1}|Tr AB|
Announced analytic route to the p-triangle inequality S_p(A+B) ≤ S_p(A)+S_p(B), 0<p<1, via an integral representation of Σα_i^p through log of the Fredholm-type product Π(1+α_i x)
ideas.modern_name: Rotfel'd trace inequality / p-normed structure of Schatten quasi-Banach classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: S. Yu. Rotfel'd (1967–69); also McCarthy (1967), R.C. Thompson (1976); determinant inequality det(1+|A+B|) ≤ det(1+|A|)det(1+|B|) (Seiler–Simon 1975)
ideas.where_published: Unsure. Possibly related material is in Produits tensoriels topologiques ch. II (operators of order p<1) or La théorie de Fredholm.

missed.claim: The theorem being proved asserts the sharp p-triangle inequality S_p(A+B) ≤ S_p(A)+S_p(B) for 0<p<1 on Schatten classes. This page and the next set up a determinant/integral proof of it. In the literature this inequality is usually credited to Rotfel'd and McCarthy around 1967; Gohberg–Krein 1965 give only a quasi-norm with a constant. If Grothendieck had a complete proof in 1953 via Π(1+α_i x) and the representation Σα_i^p = (p sin πp/π)∫ log f(x) x^{-1-p} dx, he would predate the standard attribution by over a decade. The method also anticipates the later standard 'concave function of singular values via determinants' technique.
missed.quote: La formule (3) peut être regardée comme conséquence de la formule (6) ... Une telle démonstration n'est plus utilisable pour p<1; nous démontrerons la formule (4), par voie analytique (next page)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would be a priority and attribution correction for a basic fact about quasi-Banach Schatten ideals, which is used widely in operator theory and noncommutative analysis. Whether the argument was completed has to be checked on the following pages.

deep.surprise_reason: This page itself is routine: textbook proofs of the ideal property and of the triangle inequality via duality. What raises it slightly is the context. The theorem includes the sharp p-triangle inequality for p<1, with an analytic determinant-based proof announced, and that inequality is usually attributed to work from the late 1960s. Its publication status in Grothendieck's own work is unclear.
transcription_corrections: 'les affirmations relatives aux dispositions naturelles' is likely 'aux topologies naturelles' (or 'structures naturelles') of the spaces L^p(H).

The sentence about (2) should read roughly: 'si (φ_i) diagonalise |A|, soit (α_i) la suite des valeurs propres de |A| (ou de |A*|) ... et (ψ_i) la suite des valeurs propres de |BA|, rangées par ordre de grandeur décroissante'.
'ψ_i ≤ ||B|| α_i pour tout i (dualité ...)' — the parenthetical likely cites the minimax / extremal characterization of eigenvalues rather than 'dualité'.
The final line reads sup_{||B||_{p'}≤1}|Tr AB| ≤ ||A||_p; the subscript ||B||_{p'} ≤ 1 is written beneath the sup.
On the previous page, 'L^p(A)' should be L^p(H).
